title: Wireless Phone Chargers for the Bedside: Apple MagSafe vs. Anker, Explained
subtitle: Three magnetic iPhone chargers compared on price, charging speed, and the extra parts each one needs before it works.
excerpt: A wireless charger lets you set your iPhone down instead of fiddling with a tiny plug. Here is what Apple's and Anker's chargers cost, how fast they can be, and which ones need a wall adapter you buy separately.
author: Nickel And Gadget Editors

sections.content: Plugging a phone in at night sounds simple until you are doing it in dim light with the cable end facing the wrong way. A small plug and a small port can be fiddly for anyone.

A wireless charger takes the plug out of the picture. You set the phone down on a pad, magnets pull it into place, and it starts charging. It is not magic, and it is not always fast. For a bedside table or a desk, it may be easier than lining up a plug, though none of these makers claim it helps with stiff hands or tired eyes, so that is our own reasoning.

Inside the pad is a coil that sends power to a matching coil inside your phone. On recent iPhones, a ring of magnets lines the two up so you do not have to hunt for the right spot. Apple calls its version MagSafe. Qi2 is the industry standard that works the same way, and Qi2.2 is the newer, faster version.

Speed is measured in watts. Older Qi chargers without magnets give an iPhone about 7.5 watts. Qi2 chargers give up to 15 watts, and Qi2.2 can reach 25 watts on phones that support it. The UK tech site Gadget Scout describes a 15-watt Qi2 charger as "plenty" for most people. If you charge overnight, it may be that the top speeds matter less to you, but that is our own view, not Gadget Scout's.

One honest caveat: wireless charging is slower than a good wired cable. How fast it goes also depends on the wall adapter (the plug that goes into the outlet), your phone case, and your iPhone's software version. Older iPhones get only 7.5 to 15 watts. One report, relayed by Wikipedia (a secondary source, so take it with caution), says MacRumors found Apple's charger gave iPhones older than the 12 series about half the speed of third-party 7.5-watt Qi chargers.

items: Check whether a wall adapter is in the box. Apple's MagSafe Charger and the Anker Prime station do not include one, so budget for it. Anker's MagGo Dock Stand does include its adapter.
Read the fine print on speed. The biggest wattage figures assume a separately bought adapter (Apple) or a 45-watt or larger adapter (Anker Prime), plus a recent iPhone and up-to-date software.

Match it to your phone. The Anker pages say their chargers are for iPhone and Apple Watch only and exclude Android phones. The Dock Stand page also says it is not compatible with Samsung Galaxy watches. Apple's pad also charges other Qi phones, but at a lower speed.
Mind your case. Anker says cases over 2.5 mm thick, or non-magnetic cases, may reduce charging efficiency and are not recommended.
Count your devices. If you also wear an Apple Watch or use AirPods, a 3-in-1 station puts everything in one spot.
Know the return policy. Anker lists a 30-day money-back guarantee and a warranty (the length is not stated on the page); check Apple's current return terms before buying.
Skip the add-ons. Anker's site advertises an optional paid membership, which is not needed to buy these chargers.

sections.content: Setting it up and using it well

Pick a spot near an outlet where the charger can sit flat and will not get knocked. Plug the charger's cable into the wall adapter, then into the outlet. Apple says a 20-watt adapter gives up to 15 watts on iPhone 12 or later, and a 30-watt adapter is needed for its top speed of 25 watts. For full speed on the Anker Prime, the adapter must be 45 watts or more.

Before bed, check that your iPhone software is up to date, since the Anker pages list minimum versions for full speed. Then set the phone down and let the magnets do the lining up. In the morning, the phone still has to be lifted off the pad. As a general tip, a steady hand on the base may help a light charger stay put, and Anker's FAQ addresses lifting a stand only in general terms.

Feeling some warmth is normal; Anker's FAQ says some warmth during heavy use is expected. The Dock Stand has an adjustable viewing angle, but this guide focuses on charging. If a stand is what you need, see our earlier guide to magnetic phone stands.

Your case matters as much as the charger. Anker's FAQ puts it plainly: "Cases over 2.5 mm thick or that are non-magnetic may reduce charging efficiency and are not recommended." If your phone charges slowly, try a slim MagSafe-compatible case, or test the phone with no case at all. A phone that needs to be seen from across the room is also a poor fit unless your case is magnetic.
sections.label: Before You Buy

sections.content: None of these chargers has a built-in night light, and the Anker models will not help an Android phone. But if you have a recent iPhone and are tired of fumbling with a cable in the dark, a magnetic charger is a modest, practical upgrade. Start with what you actually need, add up the adapter cost, and enjoy a calmer nightstand.

products.name: MagSafe Charger (1 m)
products.price: $39.00 (price shown on Apple's page; check current price); wall adapter sold separately
products.blurb: The simplest, lowest-cost choice for someone who only needs to charge an iPhone. It works with iPhone 8 or later. For iPhone 12 or later, Apple lists up to 15 watts with a 20-watt adapter, or up to 25 watts with a 30-watt adapter, neither of which is included.

products.name: MagGo Wireless Charging Station (3-in-1, Dock Stand)
products.blurb: A good fit for iPhone 12 or later owners who also charge an Apple Watch and AirPods, since it handles all three at once. The 40-watt wall adapter comes in the box, and the phone charges at up to 15 watts.

products.name: Prime Wireless Charging Station (3-in-1, MagGo, AirCool, Foldable)
products.price: $149.99 (sale price marked $30 off; check current price); 45W+ adapter sold separately
products.blurb: For owners of an iPhone 16 or later who want the fastest wireless speed, up to 25 watts on iOS 26 or later, plus a quiet built-in fan and a fold-up design. Earlier iPhones charge at up to 15 watts, and you must buy a 45-watt or larger adapter.
